headline: University student finds his own face on billboard as 'digital mascot' for ideology he thought was just a group chat meme
body: A second-year sociology student from Patna discovered his lecture-hall selfies have been repurposed as the viral face of a national political movement after he accidentally checked 'public domain' on a meme-generator app. The student is currently seeking legal advice to determine if he is entitled to a cut of the movement's 'influencer outreach' budget.
caption: Guess that’s one way to boost your LinkedIn profile. #Satire #SocialMediaLife #DigitalPosterBoy #PatnaDiaries (satire)
igHook: Would you sue or just lean into the fame if this happened to your profile picture?
imagePrompt: A wide shot of a brightly lit university campus hallway with students walking by, focusing on a cluttered bulletin board covered in faded flyers and event posters.

sourceHeadline.title: Swatantra Bhardwaj: How a 21-yr-old from Patna became digital poster boy of Hindutva ecosystem

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 4 stands out because it roots the satire in a grounded, relatable human mistake (checking a box on an app) rather than the generic, repetitive 'influencer bot' trope found in most other candidates. It manages to be funny and specific without relying on cynical boilerplate, providing a clear, vivid image of a student seeing his own face on a billboard.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses a generic, anonymous student as a satirical vehicle for a fictional scenario. It does not name any real individuals, target protected groups, or describe a real-world political scandal, and the image prompt is entirely generic.
